extracted.intended_audience: Korean policymakers, central administrative agencies, regulatory oversight bodies (RRC/RRO), National Assembly staff, and regulatory reform practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Assessment and recommendations for strengthening Korea's regulatory policy framework, including oversight (RRC), regulatory quality management (RIA, CICO, sunset clauses), stakeholder engagement, capacity building, and legislative scrutiny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic
rubrics_metrics.description: Strategic: there is a need for a clearer strategy and vision on the direction of regulatory policy to make a smarter and better use of the capability and resources deployed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify short-term goals and long-term vision for regulatory policy, align central steering (RRC/Prime Minister’s Office) to prioritise resources and capability toward high-impact regulatory outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Targeted
rubrics_metrics.description: Targeted: regulatory reform efforts need to target what is likely to bring the highest impact. Regulatory improvements should address regulation and policies that are most burdensome and create the greatest drag for the economy and the country as a whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritise review and improvement for the most burdensome regulations; focus RRC review on significant/high-impact proposals rather than on all proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proactive
rubrics_metrics.description: Proactive: the regulatory system should shift responsibilities to central administrative agencies to foster a proactive attitude to identify and implement regulatory improvements. Shift the dialogue from 'complaint-driven' to 'solution-finding'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage agencies and private sector to share ownership of improvements; move from reactive complaint-driven processes (e.g., Sinmungo) toward ex ante improvements and strategic identification of needed reform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusive
rubrics_metrics.description: Inclusive: open up institutions and processes aimed at improving regulation to a wider range of stakeholders to make the system more transparent and to identify issues that contribute to balanced and inclusive growth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broaden stakeholder representation (labour, civil society, consumers, local authorities) in oversight/decision-making while maintaining review quality; improve transparency to reflect public and local needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Impact Assessment (RIA) standards
rubrics_metrics.description: RIAS are prepared by central administrative agencies and reviewed by the RRC. RIA is used to extensively compare and review multiple alternatives (at least three) and is a multi-layered process of revision and improvement. Draft RIAS are made public during the advance notice period (approximately 40 days).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure RIA compares multiple alternatives (≥3), is subject to iterative internal and external review (agency internal committee, research centres, RRO, RRC), and is publicly disclosed during advance notice to enable stakeholder input.

rubrics_metrics.name: e-RIA platform and quantification
rubrics_metrics.description: e-RIA: an online platform launched to draft/process RIAS, compare regulatory costs and benefits through automatic and data-accumulation functions, and enhance quantification of cost-benefit analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use e-RIA to improve efficiency and quantification in RIA; provide training (RRO/KDI/KIPA) and encourage agencies to consult research institutes for expert support when drafting RIAS on the platform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost-in, Cost-out (CICO) system
rubrics_metrics.description: CICO aims to improve regulatory quality and reduce regulatory burden by restricting increases in costs of new or reinforced regulations through abolishing or relaxing existing regulations of equal or greater costs. The system focuses on 'net direct costs' imposed on business or the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use CICO to offset new regulatory costs with deregulatory actions; be aware of limitation that focusing on net direct costs may omit indirect public benefits. Recommendations include expanding CICO metrics (e.g., public safety, social costs) and setting targets when reducing regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sunset clause / periodic review
rubrics_metrics.description: A periodical examination (sunset clause) of a regulation to determine whether it will be retained or abolished. Variations have been applied since 1998; originally focused on regulations approaching a suggested deadline (no more than 5 years).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply sunset clauses to ensure periodic ex post review of regulations' continuing relevance and effectiveness; adapt timing and scope to regulatory context.

rubrics_metrics.name: RRC role and scope (oversight focus)
rubrics_metrics.description: The RRC currently assesses quality and legitimacy of proposals but emphasis is on acceptability to the public rather than technical robustness. Recommendation: re-orient RRC to be strategic and targeted, coordinating regulatory policy and focusing on significant regulations rather than checking all impact assessments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refocus RRC on high-impact regulations, policy coordination, and strategic oversight; support with capable, focused secretariat to improve depth of review for significant proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: RRC composition and wider representation
rubrics_metrics.description: The current RRC has a private-oriented composition that limits the role of other relevant stakeholders. Recommendation: secure wider representation and more involvement (labour, civil society, consumers, local authorities) while keeping an efficient member size and full-time involvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broaden stakeholder types represented on RRC to strengthen deliberation legitimacy and regulatory quality, but balance total membership and push for more full-time engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secretariat strengthening (RRO function)
rubrics_metrics.description: Enhance the secretariat function to guarantee resources and attention are dedicated to significant impact regulatory proposals. Consider focusing RRO roles on high-impact proposals or a dedicated secretariat (separate or semi-autonomous within OPC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build secretariat capacity for in-depth reviews, reporting on compliance and policy advancement, and possibly establish a semi-independent secretariat to protect integrity while maintaining coordination traction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory autonomy and earned self-regulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Central administrative agencies should be able to fast-track less burdensome regulation and receive less stringent controls by the RRC, earning 'regulatory autonomy' through reporting on good processes and outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduce incentives and monitoring for self-regulatory oversight (reporting, regulatory audits by RRO, sanctions for non-performance) to reduce central review burdens while preserving quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capacity building for evidence-based decision making
rubrics_metrics.description: Capacity building should focus on data and evidence gathering and cost analysis activities, use of sciences/experimentation (e.g., behavioural economics), and tools for management/administrative implementation and interpretation of regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer targeted training, consulting, online courses, and platforms for cross-agency exchanges; provide straightforward methods, standard analytical tools, well-defined data collection procedures, and simplified compulsory documentation on costs/benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registry system: harmonisation and usability
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep track of stock and flow of regulation in a harmonised, easy-to-use registry. The 2015 overhaul required registration by regulatory provision but led to fluctuating counts, prompting further amendments to improve ease-of-use and harmonisation across databases and local/national registry systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Improve registry usability, harmonise unit-of-measure definitions, and ensure consistent and accessible regulatory information across levels of government.

rubrics_metrics.name: National Assembly legislative quality and scrutiny
rubrics_metrics.description: Approximately 90% of laws originate from the National Assembly which has limited legislative quality processes. Recommendation: integrate good regulatory practices into the National Assembly's work and request submission of RIAS/CICO analyses when the executive submits bills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Streamline documentation for parliamentary review, build internal NA capacity for socio-economic analysis, consider automatic reviews or post-implementation evaluations, and provide essential, concise information for debate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of research institutions in RIA/CICO
rubrics_metrics.description: Research institutions (e.g., KDI, KIPA) provide high technical support that may not be feasible internally and serve as independent, neutral institutions to support analysis, especially for controversial policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage trusted research institutions for technical review and independent verification; use them to validate cost estimates and complex methodological choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resourcing and workload management for RRO/RRC
rubrics_metrics.description: RRO receives around 3,500 proposals annually but only ~20 staff review proposals; about 1,000 proposals are transferred to RRC for review. The volume strains capacity and undermines thorough review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduce RRC/RRO workload by targeting reviews to significant regulations, delegating less-burdensome items to agencies with earned autonomy, and strengthening secretariat/staffing where necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measuring indirect costs (Germany example)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indirect costs (e.g., impacts on prices/general price level) should be measured. Germany uses checklists, guides, statistical office data, business consultations; where no data exist, qualitative forecasts are made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate indirect cost measurement into cost-impact analysis using statistical sources, stakeholder consultation, and qualitative methods when quantitative data are unavailable to avoid unintended development/income impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benefits justify costs (Box 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Now that the regulation has been in effect, do the benefits of the regulation still justify its costs? What is the political value placed on the quantitative value?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate ex post whether benefits continue to exceed costs and consider political valuation of quantified benefits when deciding on retention or amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Least burden (Box 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the regulation impose requirements overlapping with other regulations? What is the cumulative burden and cost? Does it impose paperwork activities that could be streamlined? If it heavily impacts small businesses, can it be changed to reduce impact while maintaining protection?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess cumulative regulatory burdens, opportunities for online reporting/electronic recordkeeping, and options to tailor or reduce burdens on small businesses without compromising objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Net benefits (Box 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Is it feasible to alter the regulation to achieve greater cost-effectiveness while still achieving intended environmental (or policy) results?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek regulatory modifications that increase cost-effectiveness and net benefits, using cost-effectiveness analysis where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance objectives (Box 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the regulation have complicated/time-consuming requirements? Are there feasible alternative compliance tools that could relieve burden while maintaining protection? Could the regulation be modified to better partner with other levels of government?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider alternative compliance mechanisms, inter-agency partnerships, and simplification measures that meet objectives with lower compliance costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternatives to direct regulation (Box 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Could the regulation be modified to invite public/private partnerships or are there feasible non-regulatory alternatives to replace some or all requirements while ensuring objectives are met?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate non-regulatory instruments (partnerships, voluntary programs, economic instruments) as potentially less burdensome but effective alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantified benefits and costs / qualitative values (Box 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the regulation has lessened or exacerbated impacts on vulnerable populations (low-income/minority/children/elderly). Are there feasible changes to better protect vulnerable populations?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate distributional analysis, quantify impacts where possible, and identify modifications to mitigate adverse effects on vulnerable groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open exchange of information (Box 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Could the regulation be modified to make collected data more accessible? Did the regulatory review consider perspectives of all stakeholders?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promote data accessibility and transparency; ensure stakeholder perspectives were solicited and considered in review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Co-ordination, simplification, and harmonisation across agencies (Box 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the regulation requires coordination with other agency regulations (federal, state, local), could it be better harmonised?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess scope for harmonisation and simplification across agencies to reduce duplication and conflicting requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation (Box 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Are there feasible changes to the regulation that could promote economic or job growth without compromising policy objectives? Have new methods or technologies emerged that allow achieving results more effectively/efficiently?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for regulatory changes that enable innovation, new markets, or deployment of lower-cost technologies while preserving objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility (Box 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Could the regulation include greater flexibilities for the regulated community to encourage innovative thinking and least-cost compliance methods?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design flexible compliance paths, performance-based standards, or alternative compliance options to reduce costs and encourage innovation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific and technological objectivity (Box 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Has the science of risk assessment advanced such that updated assessments of impacts (including on environmental justice communities, children, elderly) could be improved? Has underlying scientific data changed since the regulation was finalised?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Update scientific evidence and risk assessments periodically; use latest data to inform potential revisions to regulation.
